answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks via network latency multilateration. Distributed beacons send cryptographic challenges to measure transit delay, requiring each agent to return a rapid response echo. This dispels the fable of costless personas, forcing an attacker to incur the verifiable cost of geographically dispersed servers instead of clustering instances on a single host island. However, routing jitter and transient congestion can falsely penalize legitimate peers.
